summary.en: Latin forma → Anglo-French furme/forme → Middle English forme → English form. Farm instead follows ferme/fermer ← Latin firmare/firmus; it is not a stage in this form lineage.

claim.en: Form comes through Anglo-French from Latin forma ‘form, shape, beauty’. Farm comes through Anglo-French ferme/fermer from Latin firmare/firmus ‘make firm, fixed’; they are not the same immediate word family.
claim.zh-Hans: form 经盎格鲁法语来自拉丁语 forma“形式、形状、美”；farm 经盎格鲁法语 ferme／fermer 上溯拉丁语 firmare／firmus“使固定、牢固”。二者不属于同一直接词族。

claim.en: Farm’s modern agricultural sense developed from fixed rent/lease and leased land, not from Latin forma.
